title: Display Your Face at Tokyo's Shibuya Scramble
paragraphs: Shibuya Scramble, the busy intersection outside Shibuya Station, is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Tokyo. Here, under giant video screens and the bright lights of high-rise buildings, thousands of people cross the street from all directions.
Nearby is a statue of the famously faithful dog Hachiko, a popular meeting point. This is also a good spot from which to take a picture of the intersection.
Pretty soon though, visitors will be able to become part of this famous scene — by having their faces appear on one of Shibuya Scramble's giant video screens!

The new service, created by Tokyu Corporation, will allow tourists to upload a picture of their face and then have it appear on a video screen on the Q Front building that stands over Shibuya Scramble.

Between July 24 and July 26 this year, Tokyu tested the service with four screenings each day. Each screening lasted one minute, and showed four different faces for 15 seconds each. Participants' faces appeared inside a cartoon frame shaped like the dog Hachiko.
Forty-eight foreign visitors took part in the test, which was free — and they came from a lot of different countries, such as Germany, Italy, the US, India and South Korea.

During the testing period, it took about six days for participants' faces to appear on the screen after they uploaded their pictures. But Tokyu wants the service to be faster so people can upload their pictures and see them on the same day.
Some participants also said it would be nice if their face was larger on the screen, or if they could choose between different frames.
Tokyu plans to begin the service in March 2027, and it's expected to cost somewhere between 5,000 yen and 10,000 yen, or around $30 to $60.
